answers.stem_only: The default group health check uses only EC2 status checks, so a hung application on a running instance is never seen as unhealthy; turn on ELB health checks for the group so it replaces instances that fail the target group check.
Scale horizontally: put the stateless app in an Auto Scaling group across at least two AZs behind an ALB with a target tracking policy on CPU.

Workers set instance scale-in protection on themselves while a job runs and clear it after (stops scale in from killing jobs); scale-in protection does not block manual terminations, so also enable EC2 termination protection (DisableApiTermination) to stop console terminations.
Launch configurations cannot do mixed instances or Spot plus On-Demand base; migrate to a launch template and use a mixed instances policy with an On-Demand base and several instance types.
Nothing to change: the default EC2 health checks already mark an instance that fails its system status check as unhealthy and the group replaces it.
Use a warm pool with instances in the Hibernated state: memory (the loaded data set) is preserved and only storage is paid while waiting, so scale-out is fast and cheap.
Move to target tracking (no cooldown blocking repeated scale-out) and set a default instance warmup so metrics from starting instances are not counted.
Default termination policy first picks the AZ with the most instances (A, 3 vs 2), then the instance with the oldest launch template version, so the AZ A instance from the older version.
Add a termination lifecycle hook; during Terminating:Wait copy the logs to S3, then complete the lifecycle action.
No scaling plan needed: add a predictive scaling policy directly to the Auto Scaling group and keep the target tracking policy for real-time changes.

Turn on Capacity Rebalancing so the group launches replacement Spot Instances when it gets a rebalance recommendation, before the at-risk instances are reclaimed (ideally with diversified pools / price-capacity-optimized).
Application Auto Scaling scales ECS services and DynamoDB provisioned capacity; use target tracking policies for each.
New launch template version with the patched AMI, set it on the group, start an instance refresh with minimum healthy percentage 90.
Add a subnet in AZ B (where the ALB is already enabled) to the Auto Scaling group so it balances instances across both zones.
Use a launch lifecycle hook: the instance waits in Pending:Wait, not registered with the target group, and the user data script calls CompleteLifecycleAction when done.
Externalize session state to a managed shared store (ElastiCache or DynamoDB) so any instance can serve any user.
Scheduled actions to raise capacity before the known 09:00-11:00 weekday peak and lower it after, plus a target tracking policy for unexpected rises (predictive plus target tracking would also fit).
Target tracking on backlog per instance (ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible divided by in-service instances) with acceptable backlog 60 s / 2 s = 30.
Mixed instances policy with On-Demand base capacity of 2 and Spot above the base, diversified across several instance types with the price-capacity-optimized allocation strategy.

answers.flag: B (an evening scheduled action that sets desired capacity to the night level, with predictive scaling kept) also lowers night capacity and keeps the morning peak ready; the stem does not say whether night load varies, which is the only thing that makes D clearly better.
answers.stem_only: Predictive scaling only scales out and never scales in; add a dynamic policy (target tracking) alongside it so the group scales in during the night.
Use three AZs with 3 instances each (minimum 9): losing one zone leaves 6, which is cheaper than 6 per zone in two zones (12).
No pattern to schedule or forecast, so only a dynamic target tracking policy; a few minutes of lag is accepted.
